title: Initiative app deployment contract
description:
What an app requires of whoever deploys it, published as data at env-contract.json in the app's repository root.

Every app in the set publishes one, generated from its own settings declaration and committed — because whoever reads it has a checkout, not a build. A deployment tool reads these instead of parsing each app's source, which is how a setting enforced by a validator rather than by a missing default came to be absent from the Helm chart until 2026-09-23.

The classes exist because 'required' is the distinction that misleads. An app with 131 settings and 3 mandatory ones is easy to deploy; an app that presents all 131 as configuration is not, and they look identical until someone splits them up.

service.description: The app's own name, matching its image and its repository.

public_id.description: The app's id in the Initiative App Protocol registration, for an app that registers. Absent for Initiative itself, which is what apps register WITH.

env_prefix.description: Prepended to every setting name to get the environment variable. Empty for most; initiative-billing declares lower-case fields with 'BILLING_'. Names elsewhere in this file are always the ENV NAME, already prefixed — this field is for mapping back.

required.description: The app will not start without these. Includes settings enforced by a validator, not only those lacking a default — the distinction a source parser misses.

registration.description: Credentials a third-party vendor issues when this deployment is registered there. Deferrable by construction: an app holding none of them starts anyway and serves the one route that registers it, opened by INITIATIVE_APP_SETUP_TOKEN (see src/setup.ts). A deployment tool does not need these up front, and saying so is the point of the class.

runtime.description: Read once as a FIRST-BOOT SEED, then owned by a database row and edited in the app's own settings UI. An operator needs none of these at deploy time, and a deployment tool should not carry them as deploy-time secrets: the credential-bearing ones are encrypted at rest and rotate with the app's SECRET_KEY, which a values file cannot do.

env_only.description: Operator-supplied values with no database path, so the environment is the only place to set them. These, and only these, are what a deployment tool genuinely must carry as configuration.

optional.description: Tunables whose defaults work. Present so the contract is a complete account of the app's settings rather than a list of the interesting ones.

fail_closed.description: Settings whose absence takes a whole surface dark while the service stays up. The class 'required' cannot express for a service designed to boot unconfigured — initiative-billing is the case: everything has a default, so its useful contract is what goes dark, not what is mandatory.

default_unsuitable_for_production.description: Settings with a default that is correct for a first run and wrong for a real deployment — billing's database_url points at a local SQLite file, which is data loss the first time a pod rolls. Not required, not fail-closed: silently fine until it is not.
